decisions.decision: Pre-registration is an ordering, not a document.
decisions.rationale: BENCHMARK-METHODOLOGY.md was committed in a commit containing no harness code and no number, so git log proves the analysis was not chosen after seeing the data. Three predictions held: flat node axis, no COST crossover, fixture bias dominant. Predicting the disappointing results in advance is what stops them being spun later.

decisions.decision: A fast failure is not a fast run.
decisions.rationale: Incomplete runs are excluded from makespan statistics and counted separately. This immediately surfaced a real bug: the first full run reported 19/19 incomplete at every memory rung because those workers could not fetch shard inputs. A harness that averaged failures in would have published a beautiful fictional curve.

decisions.decision: A unit living in a field name is a claim.
decisions.rationale: JobResult.grossNodeSeconds held bytes moved across the guest ABI, not seconds. The ratio was always sound, which is why verificationMultiplier needed no change, but the absolute would have been published wrong by an unguessable factor. Renamed to grossFuel/usefulFuel rather than documented — a comment does not travel with the number into a report.

decisions.decision: Publish excluded configurations with the reason, never drop them.
decisions.rationale: Real transport at 8 and 16 nodes dies on INBOUND_CONNECTION_THRESHOLD = 5 per host. Both rungs appear in an "excluded, and why" table because a rung that vanishes between the plan and the results is indistinguishable, to a reader, from one removed because its number was inconvenient.

decisions.decision: No parallel speedup is measurable in the current benchmark, and the report says so first.
decisions.rationale: Every node in both curves runs in one OS process on one JavaScript event loop, so the flat makespan across the ladder is the expected consequence rather than a finding about scaling. The scaling claim is therefore unmeasured — neither disproved nor supported. Stating this prominently is the difference between a benchmark and a brochure.

Phase 7 shipped a disagreement test whose assertions sat inside a condition that could never be true — the exact anti-pattern already listed in the handoff table. Deleting disagreement reporting entirely left all 374 node tests green. Knowing the rule did not prevent breaking it; only running the mutation caught it.

decisions.decision: Liveness changes who computes a task and when, never what the answer is.
decisions.rationale: True because a result is a pure function of (module, input, partition) and content-addressed, so every recovery action is at worst wasted work. Re-check this first if any churn code changes.

decisions.decision: A lease is a deadline, not a lock.
decisions.rationale: Nobody releases it and no keeper notices the coordinator left, so "never orphaned leases" needs no cleanup code, and resume is the same code path as start. A lock would have required the holder-liveness protocol the deadline replaces.

decisions.decision: All nodes have equal functionality; the only difference is discovery.
decisions.rationale: Stated by the owner three times because the first two applications changed the vocabulary while leaving the mechanism discriminating. Any decision keying on node kind is wrong; the only legitimate use is shared-dependency analysis over the discovery graph.

decisions.decision: Disagreement is reported, never voted on.
decisions.rationale: In execution, reduce, quorum composition and now speculation alike. At R=2 there is no majority anyway, and voting silently converts "something is wrong" into "the majority was right".

next_action: Phase 9 — public demo, consent UX and disclosure gate. Build the consent gate first, because criterion 3 forbids spending any CPU before it exists; the duty-cycle and visibility governors already exist, so what is missing is the gate and the always-visible surface. Criterion 2 is the one most likely to be quietly downgraded: the demo must run a job a person cares about the answer to, and a visitor must be able to check that answer. Two hard constraints bind this phase: DEMO-04 (no deploy workflow file may exist in the repository at all, absent rather than disabled) and vocabulary discipline (no mining/hashrate/earn/credits/tokens anywhere in the UI or the repository).
context_notes: 801 tests green across node, browser (real Chromium) and e2e projects; tsc clean; 58/72 requirements; repository public; Pages deployed by hand with no workflow file. Phase 8 published the first numbers behind a methodology committed before any harness existed. The honest headline is what the numbers cannot show: every node in both curves runs in one process on one event loop, so no parallel speedup is measurable and the scaling claim remains unmeasured. Connectivity tax 8-10x; no COST crossover, ~570x, and the decomposition attributes most of that to the guest ABI on a trivial fixture rather than to the fabric. The dominant lesson across Phases 7 and 8: a guard is worth nothing until a mutation proves it can fail, and a claim in a comment or a field name is worth nothing until the mechanism is grepped for. Both were learned by writing the anti-pattern that was already documented in the handoff file.
